entries.title: Curfew imposed in parts of central Paris and other cities after rioting across France

entries.title: Ukrainians dying because US restricting intelligence sharing, Zelensky adviser tells BBC
entries.snippet: Serhii Beskrestnov says there has not been enough time to warn people about incoming missile attacks. The White House said there had been no changes to intelligence sharing.

entries.title: Kenya cult leader who told parents to starve children guilty of 191 murders

entries.title: Five ways El Niño is affecting the weather around the world

entries.title: US airman dies as daredevil descent goes wrong before Texas college football game

entries.snippet: Obama says federal agents' search of the Democrat's home was an effort to intimidate a Trump critic.

entries.snippet: The blaze that killed four men and injured dozens of others spread with alarming speed, accounts suggest.

entries.title: Possible wreckage of Amelia Earhart's plane likely to be trees, say researchers
entries.snippet: Researchers travelled to a remote Pacific Island to confirm whether an object first spotted on satellite imagery in 2020 solved the mystery of the pilot's disappearance.

entries.title: Catalonia's former rebel president can return to Spain, court rules
entries.snippet: The court upholds a decision to lift an arrest warrant for Carles Puigdemont linked to the independence bid he led in 2017.

entries.title: Italy plans tougher security measures after violent protests
entries.snippet: The government crackdown comes after protests over rising costs broke out into violent clashes.

entries.snippet: The US president blocked numerous sanctions on Russia two days before they were due to take effect.

entries.title: Bangladesh says it was not informed of its citizens' execution by Saudi Arabia
entries.snippet: Saudi Arabia said it executed two Bangladeshis last week for committing an "indecent act" in a mosque.

entries.title: Bollywood actor Tiger Shroff survives shooting attempt in Mumbai
entries.snippet: Videos showed gunmen firing shots at Shroff's car while it was moving slowly past a crowd.

entries.title: Judge chastises Trump administration plan to push ahead overhaul of DC golf course
entries.snippet: The Trump administration wants to turn a historic public golf course into championship links. Despite a judge's order, hundreds of trees were cut down to make way for the renovation.

entries.title: Schools struggle to measure how much AI experiments are helping
entries.snippet: Schools are experimenting with AI, and a lot of them are encountering the same problem: It's hard to measure whether the technology is good or bad for students.

entries.title: Australian prime minister says lawmaker critically injured by car is 'no accident'
entries.snippet: A car hit an Australian federal independent lawmaker on Monday, critically injuring her in an apparent deliberate attack, Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said. The driver was arrested.

entries.snippet: Hint: It's not only because California counts slowly.

entries.title: A Kelvin wave raised sea levels on the West Coast. More are coming
entries.snippet: A large underwater wave moved up the West Coast, raising sea levels. Scientists say it's driven by El Niño and it's going to happen again.

entries.title: Michigan's Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed campaigns in GOP stronghold
entries.snippet: Michigan's Democratic U.S. Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed is campaigning in the GOP stronghold of Michigan's Upper Peninsula, an area that hasn't voted for a Democrat in Congress in over a decade.

entries.title: Solar power is changing agriculture in Pakistan, but some fear it could cause issues
entries.snippet: Solar power is transforming agriculture in Pakistan. But in a country already facing water scarcity and extreme weather, some fear their widespread use could cause problems.

entries.title: Alberta voters weigh future in Canada
entries.snippet: On Monday voters in the oil-rich Canadian province of Alberta are deciding whether to take the first step toward a future referendum on independence.

entries.title: Minnesota teen accused of plotting terror attack at Mall of America to remain jailed
entries.snippet: Authorities have said the attack was thwarted by FBI agents after they monitored the 18-year-old for nearly two years and ultimately supplied him with the AK-47 he planned to use.

entries.title: On 'Settle In,' Kathryn Jezer-Morton and Geoff Bennett discuss social media's impact
entries.snippet: Social media lets us share our lives with family, friends, and strangers. But how do people decide what to post, what to leave out, and what do those decisions say about them? On "Settle In," Geoff Bennett discusses that with Kathryn Jezer-Morton, author of "The Story of Your Lif

entries.title: Mississippi attorney general says officer's force was justified in death of 1-year-old Kohen Wiley
entries.snippet: Mississippi's attorney general says a Senatobia officer was justified in using force when he responded to a shoplifting call and fired at a moving vehicle that investigators said was driving toward police, killing a boy who was in the car.

entries.title: From France to Albania, how social unrest is fueling protests across Europe
entries.snippet: Rising food and fuel prices, a lack of funding for education, the state of public services, and access to housing have created the perfect breeding ground for a fall of protests across Europe.

entries.title: Activist Mahmoud Khalil asks Supreme Court to let judges quickly reverse immigration detentions
entries.snippet: Khalil, a lawful permanent U.S. resident, was detained by immigration authorities last year because of his participation in pro-Palestinian demonstrations at Columbia University in the spring of 2024.

entries.title: Japan launches spacecraft to Mars' moon in mission to bring back soil samples
entries.snippet: Five of the world's space agencies have joined forces for the five-year mission that will attempt to land a robotic prospector plus a rover on Phobos, the larger of Mars' two moons.

entries.title: Ex-OpenAI worker accused of bugging conference room planned to fly to Saudi Arabia, prosecutors say
entries.snippet: Prosecutors have not said what Abdulrahman Alfozan, a 35-year-old Saudi national, might have wanted to do with the recordings, but say he was in "frequent communication" with a member of the Saudi royal family.

entries.title: A bitter Michigan Senate race rattles Jewish and Muslim voters already on edge over the war in Gaza
entries.snippet: Michigan's closely contested Senate race has become deeply personal for some voters.

entries.title: Homeland Security grants temporary deportation reprieve for more than 100,000 Ukrainians and Sudanese
entries.snippet: This decision comes as activists and lawmakers argue there are no safe conditions for Ukrainians to return to amid the war with Russia.

entries.title: AP source: Eagles QB Jalen Hurts expected to miss rest of season after blood clots found in lungs and leg
entries.snippet: Hurts has deep vein thrombosis and a bilateral pulmonary emboli, meaning a clot has traveled from his legs to his lungs.

entries.title: Longtime CNN anchor Christiane Amanpour leaving network after a storied career of 43 years
entries.snippet: Amanpour's exit coincides with a new era at CNN as it comes under new owner Skydance, after an $81 billion merger that brings CNN and CBS under one roof.

entries.title: DW
entries.snippet: News, Analysis and Service from Germany and Europe - in 30 Languages

entries.title: France: Partial curfews imposed in Paris, Nice after unrest
entries.snippet: French authorities imposed curfews in towns and cities on Monday night after cost-of-living and anti-government protests descended into rioting and looting over the weekend. DW has the latest.

entries.title: Bulgaria seeks suspects in Germany after Starlink sabotage
entries.snippet: A Bulgarian court has issued arrest warrants for two young German nationals suspected of setting fire to Starlink antennas. The case is reminiscent of another in Poland, which Warsaw says was orchestrated by Russia.

entries.title: Germany news: Emergency at Leipzig airport sparked by novice driver
entries.snippet: Two men breached a fence at the Leipzig/Halle airport while practicing for a driving test. Meanwhile, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz announced an industrial AI partnership with Nvidia. DW has more.

entries.title: Kenya: Cult leader guilty of murdering 190 children, 1 adult
entries.snippet: Preacher Paul Mackenzie was accused of encouraging his followers to starve themselves to death. He ran a Christian doomsday cult called the Good News International Church that claimed the end of the world was imminent.

entries.title: Canada: Alberta votes on holding independence referendum
entries.snippet: Canada's oil-rich western province of Alberta is not deemed likely to vote in favor of a real breakaway plebiscite. Nevertheless the separatist movement hopes to gain leverage over Mark Carney's government.

entries.title: Can diplomacy stop another Ethiopia-Eritrea war?
entries.snippet: Ethiopia has installed a new administration in conflict-hit Tigray after federal forces pushed back Tigrayan fighters. But tensions with Eritrea continue to raise fears of a wider regional war.

entries.title: Houthi strike on Yemen government military camp kills at least 50
entries.snippet: The Iran-backed group has claimed responsibility for the attack which killed new recruits at a military camp. The strikes follow deadly attacks over the weekend blamed on Saudi-led forces.

entries.title: Rubio visits India with a trip to the world's largest oil refinery topping the agenda
entries.snippet: A visit to India this week by Washington's top diplomat will skip New Delhi and instead include the world's largest oil refinery, which processes massive amounts of Russian crude. Is Trump looking for a new deal?

entries.title: Myanmar refugees find hope in Thailand's work program
entries.snippet: A year ago, Thailand granted long-staying refugees from Myanmar the right to work legally. Refugees and rights groups welcome the move but say the program's first year has exposed significant shortcomings.

entries.title: UN food program cuts aid to 500,000 Palestinians in Gaza
entries.snippet: Amid funding shortages, the World Food Program has said it is being forced to reduce necessary aid. Over two-thirds of Palestinians in Gaza are facing acute hunger, according to the agency.

entries.title: From delivery driver to global fame: A Korean writer's journey
entries.snippet: You Yeong-Gwang's The Rainfall Market tells the story of a mysterious, hidden shop that only opens when it rains. For a debut novel by an unknown author, it was a massive success.

entries.title: The homeless man living in front of a London mega-mansion
entries.snippet: Anders Fernstedt lives in London without any money. The Swedish native has built a most unusual home under the porch of a house worth over €200 million. How did that happen?

entries.title: Greece: At least 12 die in migrant drownings overnight
entries.snippet: Authorities say 12 people, including an infant, have drowned in Greek waters in two separate incidents overnight. Another 22 people were rescued. A search-and-rescue operation is ongoing.

entries.title: Australian MP seriously hurt in suspected car attack
entries.snippet: Helen Haines, an independent federal lawmaker, has been struck by a car in what Australia's prime minister has called an apparent attack.

entries.title: Ukraine got 'no warning' of Russian ballistic strikes, Zelenskyy says
entries.snippet: Massive strikes overnight hit the capital Kyiv, and damaged power stations, killing at least one person and cutting power to hundreds of thousands.

entries.title: West Bank: Israel arrests 10 suspects over settler attacks on US journalist, European diplomats
entries.snippet: Israeli police made the arrests following attacks on a US journalist and European diplomats in the occupied West Bank. Israeli human rights group Yesh Din has reported at least 170 settler attacks since September 27.

entries.title: Deepfakes, bots and distrust: How AI is shaping Israel's election
entries.snippet: For the first time, AI is playing a major role in Israel's elections. Observers warn that deepfakes, bots and influence campaigns could sway voters.

entries.title: India news: CJP alleges 'deliberate' delay in leaders' release
entries.snippet: CJP leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were due to be released on Sunday. The judge in the case has recused himself after claiming that he was threatened.

entries.title: Brazil: Lula, Bolsonaro clash in heated presidential debate
entries.snippet: The candidates traded barbs, including over Bolsonaro's ties to US President Donald Trump in their first debate, days before the October 25 election runoff.
